title: Structured Output + Function Calling Walkthrough - Aurelia Analytics
meeting_header: 2025-01-28 14:00 UTC • 54 minutes • Redwood: Samira, Diego, Jordan • Aurelia: Marcus, Lena, Oliver, Priya
summary: AE+SE walkthrough of Redwood API/Console/Optimize focused on structured JSON output (JSON-mode), function/tool calling and guardrails. Customer is evaluating hosted vs private for a pilot that needs strict schema validation, PII redaction, and auditability. Discussed sample schema design, server-side validation, and how Console shows structured outputs and rollouts. Agreed to run a 2-week pilot with a JSON-mode schema and request Docker benchmark for on-prem latency. Action: send demo recording, security pack, pilot SOW draft.
topics: JSON-mode / structured output and schema enforcement
Function/tool calling for downstream system actions
Guardrails: validation, rate limits, hallucination mitigation
Console demo: route config, schema editor, Optimize suggestions
transcript:
[00:00:01] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Samira on AE and Diego's our solutions engineer today. We have like 50 minutes, we'll jump into a JSON-mode demo that shows structured output and tool calling.

[00:00:15] Marcus: Thanks. Quick ask up front — our main requirement is that the model output fits a tight schema before it hits downstream billing systems. We need validation and an audit trail.

[00:00:30] Diego: Totally, that's exactly what we'll demo. We'll show the API with JSON-mode where you define a schema for the response, Redwood's runtime will enforce and return a structured payload, and the Console will surface any schema mismatches as errors so you get visibility.

[00:00:45] Lena: When you say 'enforce' do you mean the model is blocked from returning free text? Our pipeline needs guaranteed field types — e.g., numeric invoice_total, iso8601 date, and a nested items array.

[00:01:00] Diego: Right — there are two levers. One is schema-constrained generation where we bias tokens to match the schema and validate post-hoc. If there's a mismatch we can either reject the response, sanitize it, or fallback to a looser variant. In Console you choose the policy per route.

[00:01:20] Jordan: And Optimize will suggest settings — batching, temperature, and quantization profile — based on your prompt traffic so you don't blow budget while keeping quality.

[00:01:30] Oliver: What's the latency hit for schema enforcement? We care about 95th percentile under 300ms for short calls.

[00:01:40] Diego: For hosted small requests, JSON-mode validation + light re-rolls usually add 20–80ms depending on sequence length. If you need stricter guarantees we recommend Dedicated pools or Private with lower variance. We'll show a console trace.

[00:02:05] Samira: I'll share my screen — opening the Console route we pre-configured for 'invoice_extractor_demo'. It's set to JSON-mode with a schema. You can see the schema editor here.

[00:02:20] Marcus: Can you show an example schema?

[00:02:25] Diego: Sure — in the editor we modeled it like: 'invoice_id: string, invoice_total: number, issued_at: datetime, items: array of { sku: string, qty: integer, price: number }'. We also added a PII flag on 'customer_email' so Optimize can recommend redaction patterns.

[00:02:45] Lena: Are we able to attach JSON Schema drafts? We use draft-07 across infra.

[00:02:52] Jordan: Console supports importing a JSON Schema (draft-04/06/07) and will compile it down to the runtime constraints. You can also link test prompts for the eval harness.

[00:03:05] Priya: How do we handle partial outputs? Like if the model returns a missing 'items' array?

[00:03:12] Diego: You set the route policy — reject and log as validation_error, or accept with defaults. Common pattern is to reject in prod and in dev allow auto-fill. Either way, Console creates an audit entry with the original raw output, the attempted structured parse, and the validation verdict.

[00:03:30] Marcus: Good. Show us the tool calling/ function call flow — we want the model to trigger downstream actions like 'create_invoice' only after schema validated.

[00:03:40] Diego: We'll demo a function calling flow. In the API you register an action schema and a webhook. The model can return a structured intent like: action: 'create_invoice', payload: { invoice_id: ..., total: ... }. Redwood can do an automated pre-validation step then POST to your webhook or hold it for manual approval.

[00:04:00] Lena: Do you provide retries and dead-letter handling?

[00:04:05] Diego: Yes — retry policies, exponential backoff, and DLQ support for failing calls. All surfaced in the Console under 'Integrations' with per-route delivery metrics.

[00:04:20] Oliver: Security — where's the webhook executed from? We need private endpoints inside our VPC.

[00:04:26] Jordan: For Private deployments the connector can be inside your VPC; for Hosted we provide a secure outbound egress IP range and support mTLS and static IPs. We also have KMS integrations so payloads can be encrypted in transit and at rest.

[00:04:40] Marcus: SOC 2 and audit logs?

[00:04:43] Samira: We are SOC 2 Type II and have audit logging; Console exposes token-level usage, request/response pairs (redacted per policy), and immutable export for compliance. We'll attach our compliance pack after the call.

[00:04:55] Priya: Could you walk through an end-to-end prompt -> schema -> function call?

[00:05:00] Diego: Absolutely. I'll run a live example using the API playground. Prompt: 'Extract invoice fields from the following email...' The runtime returns a structured object that matches the editor schema. If it matches, Redwood annotates it 'validated: true' and triggers the 'create_invoice' webhook. If not, it surfaces the validation errors.

[00:05:25] [DEMO - typing sounds]

[00:05:40] Diego: Ok here's a sample response (reading): invoice_id: 'INV-2025-001', invoice_total: 12,340.50, issued_at: 2025-01-22T18:03:00Z, items: [ { sku: 'SKU-11', qty: 3, price: 4120.166 } ] — Console shows 'validated: true' and a green delivery row for the webhook.

[00:06:05] Lena: I hear a decimal that looks like a float rounding — can we force integer cents instead of float dollars?

[00:06:10] Diego: Yes, that's a schema choice — define 'invoice_total_cents' as integer. Optimize can flag fields that are numeric but inconsistent across outputs.

[00:06:25] Marcus: In some of our legacy flows we need a safety net: redact sensitive fields before they leave Redwood. How does that work?

[00:06:33] Jordan: The Console has a redact pipeline where you tag fields as 'PII' and choose redaction mode — mask, drop, or hash. For hosted routes we provide runtime redaction; for Private you can run local redaction logic pre-delivery.

[00:06:48] Priya: What about hallucination where model invents an invoice_id? Is there a best practice?

[00:06:55] Diego: Two things — add strong schema constraints (pattern match for invoice IDs), and cross-check against your system using function calling: if the model returns 'create_invoice' we'll call a small verification endpoint that checks ID uniqueness before commit. Also run regular evals with your prompt sets via Console to detect regressions.

[00:07:15] Marcus: Can Optimize automatically recommend decreasing temperature or switching to a deterministic decode for sensitive routes?

[00:07:20] Jordan: Yep — Optimize analyzes prompt variance and suggests temp=0 or nucleus adjustments per route. It will also propose quantization when we see batch patterns to cut cost.

[00:07:35] [Some cross-talk: agreement]

[00:07:45] Oliver: For the pilot we need an on-prem latency benchmark. Can you give us a Docker image or AMI to run?

[00:07:52] Samira: We have a Private package and can provide a trial Docker bundle for the inference runtime plus a config that mirrors your schema. We'll coordinate with Diego to hand off the SOW.

[00:08:05] Lena: Licensing question — what's the pricing for schema-enforced calls? Is it the same per token?

[00:08:12] Samira: Pricing is token-based for Hosted; for Dedicated we do a predictable committed capacity model and for Private it's a license plus support and infra. We can send an example pricing sheet and a pilot quote.

[00:08:25] Marcus: Competitors — we've looked at provider X and Y; how do you compare for enterprise controls?

[00:08:30] Samira: Many competitors focus on raw generation APIs. Redwood's differentiator is production-grade controls: schema enforcement, audit logs, native function calling, and clear performance tradeoffs. We also have dedicated enterprise features like VPC private connectors and KMS integrations.

[00:08:45] Priya: Ok let's talk timeline — we want a 2-week pilot starting mid-Feb, then production by end of Q2 if metrics look good.

[00:08:55] Samira: That works. Diego — I'll hand it to you to capture scope.

[00:09:00] Diego: Capture: pilot includes 2-week hosted pilot with JSON-mode route, sample schema, webhook integration to Aurelia dev endpoint, 1 day of SE support for onboarding, evaluation metrics dashboard in Console. We'll also provide a Docker bundle for latency tests.

[00:09:20] Marcus: Can you show one more thing — how the Console surfaces bad generations so our product reviewers can triage?

[00:09:27] Diego: Sure — under Route Insights you get a timeline with validation_errors. Click an item and you see side-by-side: user prompt, raw model text, parsed JSON attempt, and validation diffs. You can annotate and create a ticket that exports to Jira.

[00:09:45] [Long pause while Diego navigates]

[00:10:05] Lena: I noticed in the Console trace there's a token-level cost breakdown. Can we map that back to product features?

[00:10:12] Jordan: Yes — Console gives token counts per step: prompt, prefix cache hits, model decode. Optimize correlates cost vs accuracy on your eval set so you can pick tradeoffs.

[00:10:25] Marcus: Anything we should be cautious about?

[00:10:30] Diego: The usual — schema drift over time, prompt drift. We recommend scheduled evals and synthetic prompt injection. Console supports scheduled evals and alerting on regression.

[00:10:44] Priya: Great — let's summarize next steps.

[00:10:48] Samira: Recap: We'll send the security/compliance pack and the demo recording. Diego will draft a short pilot SOW and provide the Docker latency bundle. Jordan will schedule a 45-minute technical on-prem benchmark session w/ Oliver and Lena. We'll aim to start the pilot week of Feb 17.

[00:11:10] Marcus: Perfect. Also please include an example JSON Schema and a short doc on redaction controls in the pack.

[00:11:18] Samira: Will do. Thanks all — we'll follow up in email.

[00:11:22] [Meeting ends — 54 minutes total, recording stops]
